I think that upvoat and downvoat limits are a good idea, although the particular limits may need tweaking.

Until recently, people could notice when they had reached their limits because the voats didn't 'stick'. If they refreshed the page, the up/down triangles went back to the 'haven't voated' state. Recently (2 days ago?) this has changed. Now the triangles change color as if you have voated, but the voats have no effect. I'll call this "placebo voating" after the close door buttons they put in elevators that have no purpose other to placate impatient people.

We shouldn't do this. It feels deceptive, in the same way as shadowbanning, although obviously not as severe.

Instead, we should have an indicator somewhere that shows when people have hit their voating limit.
Voating limits are great, but I suggest a clear indication of when they count or not. "Placebo voating" has too many similarities with shadowbanning.
Close door buttons do something--but only if the elevator is in the correct mode. In standard operation, they don't do anything.
